item.description: - Meeting Privacy no longer turns on by itself during calls. To blur private windows automatically in every call, turn it on in Settings › Meeting Privacy. - The tour now shows Meeting Privacy with a switch, so you can turn automatic blur on or off right there. - The shortcuts that cover the window in front or every private app work as before.

- New gesture tour: one gesture per step, with a preview of the move and a test area where you try it yourself. Next unlocks once you've done the gesture, Skip tour is always there, and closing the window pauses the tour so it picks up where you left off. - Butterfly now has an icon in the Dock. Click it to open Settings, right-click for Pause tiling and the tour. Turn it off in Settings › General › Show in Dock. - The strip map stays on screen longer after a swipe: 2 seconds by default, adjustable from 0.5 to 5 seconds in Settings › Strip & Windows › Map stays. - Meeting Privacy no longer covers a whole full-screen browser during a call. Glass stays only on private windows of the current Space and comes back when you return to the desktop.

- New: change any shortcut. Open Settings › Shortcuts, click a shortcut and press the new keys. Esc cancels, Delete removes it, ↺ brings one row back. - New shortcut presets: Butterfly (as before), AeroSpace style (⌥ instead of ⌃⌥) and Hyper key (for Caps Lock set up as ⌃⌥⇧⌘ in Karabiner, Raycast or BetterTouchTool). - Essentials at the top of Settings › Shortcuts: the shortcuts people use most, in one place. - Butterfly warns before a new shortcut collides: with another Butterfly shortcut (Replace), with macOS (for example Mission Control), or with ⌥ + letter, which types special characters. - The tour, tips and menus show your current shortcuts. - Butterfly now offers to move itself to Applications when opened from the disk image or Downloads, so updates keep working. - Overview opens on an empty workspace too, with a "No windows in this workspace" note and the workspace pills, so you can switch from there. With only one workspace and no windows, a short hint tells you to open an app. - Overview bends evenly around the middle of the screen, whichever window has focus.
